solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dangerous movement in which Linda's led astray

indicators.note: led astray means sent off course, so the letters of the words before it wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning about a risky manoeuvre during which Linda has been misled.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden collapse of earth and rock down a slope is a hazardous shifting of ground.

indicators.note: reducing the phrase flab ourselves cuts it down to a run of letters hidden inside it

explanation.surface: Losing our own flab is a heroic effort worthy of Hercules.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'reducing' with 'flab' as dieting; here it trims the phrase to the letters running from the end of flab into ourselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelve tasks of Hercules are traditionally called his labours, so a huge piece of work fits.

indicators.note: unusually says the name Diana is to appear in an unusual arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: The goddess Diana is, unusually, showing a natural, unaffected character.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a water nymph is a nature spirit living in springs, rivers and lakes.

clue.text: Female group of stars getting regular payments

parts.note: Sal is a woman's name, short for Sally or Sarah
Aries, the Ram, is a constellation of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A women's pop band earning a steady wage.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixed pay, usually monthly, for salaried staff comes at regular intervals.

clue.text: After coffee, perhaps, respond about a film repeat

indicators.note: after says the second piece is placed following the coffee piece

parts.note: instant coffee is one kind of coffee, so an example of the word instant

indicators.note: about means the word for respond goes around the letter A

parts.note: to respond is to reply

explanation.surface: Someone, after a cup of coffee, answers a question about a rerun of film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like the time of day for the surface's coffee break; it orders the pieces, coffee's kind first. A film repeat here means a television sports rerun.
explanation.definitionFit: In sports broadcasting the immediate rerun of footage of an incident is this kind of replay.

definitions.meaning: Anthony ... was British Prime Minister 1955 to 1957
the biblical garden where Adam and Eve lived, a heavenly place

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister's idea of heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden was a postwar Prime Minister, and the garden of Genesis is the byword for paradise.

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A girl whose father has got married.
explanation.definitionFit: Pam, short for Pamela, is a girl's name, so it serves as an example of one.

clue.text: Insult: what you can't do to a good book!

definitions.meaning: a cutting remark that belittles someone

definitions.text: what you can't do to a good book!
definitions.meaning: a book you can't stop reading is one you can't lay aside on the table

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the noun into a two-word phrase: a gripping book is one you cannot put down.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting remark that humiliates someone is a noun for an insult, and the split phrase means to set something aside.

indicators.note: wrestling twists and contorts, so the letters of try arm are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to try arm wrestling, with a victim in prospect.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who suffers or dies for a cause is a sacrificial sufferer, hence a victim.

definitions.meaning: informal British slang, short for brilliant
a European flatfish related to the turbot

explanation.definitionFit: Short for brilliant in British slang, and also the name of a flatfish similar to the turbot.

clue.text: Female lieutenant going to monarch for protection

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A woman officer approaches the sovereign seeking safety.
explanation.definitionFit: A place of refuge or cover gives protection from danger or weather.

parts.note: beneath means under
a way is a road or street, as in Broadway

explanation.surface: Something moving forward below a city road, like an underground train.
explanation.definitionFit: Once a project has started and is moving ahead, it is said to be in progress.

indicators.note: spinning turns the chosen letters around so they read backwards
fifty percent of an eight-letter word is half of it, here its closing half

explanation.surface: A politician spinning a story that is half nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: '50 percent of' takes the last four letters of tommyrot, YROT, and 'spinning' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of Britain's Conservative Party is a politician of the right.

indicators.note: confused means the letters of the words before it are mixed up into another order

explanation.surface: Lee's grandmother, in a muddle, loses her temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'blows up' as losing one's temper; it means makes bigger, as with a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a photograph is to make a bigger print of it, increasing its size.

clue.text: Her ten giant blunders constituting a menace

indicators.note: the letters of the words before it blunder about, ending up in a different order

explanation.surface: Her ten giant mistakes add up to a real danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that poses a danger or warns of harm is menacing, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Article 21 in shed, an alternative to 8?

indicators.note: in means the article and the short form go inside the word for shed

parts.note: a hut is a small shed
a is the indefinite article
the answer to 21 across is abbreviated Lib, as in Lib Dem

explanation.surface: A cryptic object placed in a garden shed is offered as a substitute for another clue's answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 across is a flatfish, so the definition asks for another flatfish; the question mark marks it as an example. Liberal is abbreviated in British politics, as in Lib Dem.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are large edible flatfish, so one could be chosen in place of the other at the fishmonger.

definitions.meaning: to signal or mean, as in a red sky signals rain
periods of time, as in a spell of office

explanation.definitionFit: To signify a consequence is one verb sense, and periods of duty or office are another, plural noun sense.

clue.text: Marshy ground, not exactly level at first, for plant

parts.note: a fen is low-lying marshland, as in East Anglia's Fens

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Boggy, uneven ground is suitable for growing a herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes the initials of not, exactly and level, giving NEL, though the surface reads 'not exactly level' as uneven.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall aromatic herb of the carrot family, grown for its bulb, seeds and leaves.

clue.text: Canvassing part of tent as one speaks

indicators.note: as one speaks says the word for part of a tent is to be pronounced, giving a word that sounds identical

parts.note: a tent pole holds the canvas up

explanation.surface: Canvas is part of a tent, and canvassing goes on while someone talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as one speaks' asks for a word sounding like POLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Canvassing opinion is surveying people, and a survey of opinion is called by this word.

clue.text: Witty remarks from salesman, skill and energy doubled

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative
art is skill, as in the art of conversation

indicators.note: doubled means the letter for energy is written twice

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A salesman's banter, with his skill and energy redoubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick, clever exchange of banter or ripostes in conversation.

definitions.meaning: the Sappers are the Royal Engineers, abbreviated RE, with the definite article in front

explanation.walkthrough: Sappers is the nickname of the Royal Engineers, the army corps abbreviated RE; put the definite article in front of that abbreviation and it reads as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: If you are present at an event you are said to have been at that place, present.

clue.text: Collector of folk tales, mostly unpleasant

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the collector's name is used

parts.note: the Brothers Grimm collected German fairy and folk tales

explanation.surface: A folklorist who was largely disagreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of GRIMM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidding, gloomy or harsh is unpleasant to face.

indicators.note: an interpretation of the word braille reads its letters a different way, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A kind, broad-minded reading of a text in raised dots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interpretation of' suggests loose reading, as in a liberal interpretation; here it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A liberal helping is a lavish one, so the word means open-handed or plentiful.

definitions.meaning: the putting area around the hole on a golf course

explanation.definitionFit: Inexperience is described by this colour, and the smooth putting surface on a golf course bears the same name.

definitions.meaning: took a seat, as in she rested on the bench

explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of a verb for being seated, and the standard short form of Saturday.

clue.text: A month in addition? Why not, I suppose

parts.note: May is a month of the year
as well means in addition or too

explanation.surface: Someone agreeing to an extra month off, reluctantly.
explanation.definitionFit: A grudging agreement that one might do something since there is no reason not to.
